A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original channel-generation experiments on modified 3GPP, QuaDRiGa and DeepMIMO data, including parameter-generation, reconstruction and generalization results in Section 6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their outcomes, including Figures 5–6 and 11–13 and Table 13.

M1.justification: The AmbientGAN, CSVAE and CSGMM procedures, architectures and model extensions are unchanged. The correction in Equation (30) affects an additive term involving fixed observation-noise variance, so optimization over model parameters is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use modified 3GPP and DeepMIMO for SIMO, QuaDRiGa 5G-Urban and 5G-Rural for OFDM, and Large-Urban for configuration generalization. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparisons with M-SBL, AmbientGAN for s, AmbientGAN for h and ground truth. Appendix F also retains the same Kronecker-constrained CSVAE and CSGMM comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendices D–F retain the same preprocessing, pilot selection, sample budgets, system configurations, hyperparameter selection and evaluation metrics. No experimental protocol is revised.

E4.justification: The training-sample and delay/Doppler-bound sensitivity experiments remain unchanged. Appendix F retains the same configuration-generalization, path-count and Kronecker-covariance analyses, alongside the same generated-sample illustrations.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point estimates, curves and histograms. Neither reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests, and no seed or repeated-run information is added.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative experimental results match, including Figures 5–6 and 11–13. For example, Table 13 retains 5G-Urban evaluation nMSE values of 0.00109 and 0.00096 for CSGMM trained on 5G-Urban and Large-Urban, respectively.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4, Equation (30), changes M log(sigma_i^2) to -M log(sigma_i^2) inside the second subtracted bracket. This corrects the cancellation of noise-normalization terms in the CSVAE derivation; the other definitions, assumptions and derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph and conclusion retain the same claims about learning from corrupted observations, physical interpretability and consistency, generalization without retraining, and SBGM's advantages over implicit models.

C2.justification: The explanations of sparsity, physical consistency and experimental behavior are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same limitations concerning non-stationary channels, off-grid mismatches and OFDM pilot patterns.

D1.justification: v3 adds a source-code repository pointer in footnote 1 on page 2, absent from v2. The implementation, hyperparameter, hardware and pseudocode disclosures in the appendices are otherwise unchanged. Repository contents cannot be assessed from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is unchanged, but Section 2 removes the explicit statement that Baur et al. (2024b) and Fesl et al. (2023) do not consider channel parameters. This slightly reduces the stated distinction from those studies while retaining the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 condenses introductory and related-work prose, lightly edits the contribution paragraph, and adjusts affiliation wording and spacing. The section order and overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: The new code footnote and shortened prose slightly reflow page 2; the affiliation block and subsequent footnote numbering also change. Figures and tables retain their placement, structure, captions, axes and legends.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects a mathematical sign error in Appendix A.4 and adds a concrete source-code location, improving mathematical accuracy and reproducibility guidance. The empirical evidence and core claims remain unchanged, so the gains are limited. The shortened related-work distinctions do not materially outweigh these benefits.
